title: The gerund: two actions at once

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the *gerundio* for actions that happen at the same time from B1 Unit 2. The gerund (*-ando*, *-iendo*) tells us how or while the main action happens. Movements are often described this way: *marchaban gritando consignas*.

items.spanish: Los obreros marchaban por las calles gritando consignas.
items.english: The workers marched through the streets shouting slogans.

items.spanish: Los campesinos pedían tierra, uniéndose en asociaciones.
items.english: The peasants asked for land, joining together in associations.

items.spanish: Los estudiantes protestaban escribiendo periódicos y haciendo reuniones.
items.english: The students protested by writing newspapers and holding meetings.

items.spanish: El Frente Sandinista luchaba contra el gobierno, recibiendo el apoyo de muchos grupos.
items.english: The Sandinista Front fought against the government, receiving the support of many groups.

sections.content: The gerund has the same subject as the main verb and never changes: *marchaban gritando*. Attached pronouns go at the end: *uniéndose*, with an accent mark.
